problem: VLM-based embodied navigation lacks aligned open-world vision-and-control data, and RL trained from scratch or in photorealistic simulators suffers from cold-start, sample inefficiency and poor Sim2Real transfer.
motivation: Humans rehearse plans via mental simulation in simplified abstractions before acting. The paper distills a large VLM's reasoning into a small policy through cheap, physics-constrained semantic sandbox tasks and experience rules instead of costly real-world exploration.
key_idea: Synthesize tasks and IF-THEN experience rules in a physics-grounded semantic sandbox (HM3D + InteriorGS), then train a small VLM with GRPO using hybrid experience-augmented sampling and asymmetric adaptive clipping, and deploy it as a frontier/memory-node selector on top of a geometric planner.
insight: Most of the gain comes from sandbox-synthesized tasks (+Task: 43.51→50.71 SR† on A-EQA at 2B), with experience rules, AAC and inference-time retrieval adding smaller consistent gains. Retrieval relevance matters: mismatched experience drops A-EQA SR† to 44.88, and random experience gives 51.73 vs 53.21. Annealing the experience-injection probability and a relaxed but finite upper clip (ε_exp=1.0; 0.4 underfits, 1.2 is unstable) balance imitation and generalization.
method: Genesis (task synthesis): sample start-goal pairs in navigable space, compute A* geodesic trajectories, render 3 views (0°, ±120°) at keypoints, and have Qwen3-VL-Plus produce language queries and answers over 8 EQA task categories from detected objects and a scene graph; 14,526 valid trajectories (7,988 HM3D + 6,538 InteriorGS) after rejection sampling.
Genesis (experience rules): prompt the VLM to explain why the forward view was chosen over other frontiers as IF-THEN rules, stored in a vector database D_exp.
Reward shaping: format-compliance reward plus correct-image-selection indicator scaled by (1 + Rouge-L similarity), minus an error penalty (w_f=0.1, w_acc=1.0, P_err=0.5).

Hybrid prompt-augmented sampling: retrieved rules are injected with Bernoulli probability η_t, annealed from 0.8 toward 0 as best validation reward approaches the target 1.5; GRPO groups are homogeneous in mask so advantages are normalized within augmented or standard groups.
Asymmetric Adaptive Clipping: lower clip fixed at 1-ε_std (0.2) for all samples, upper clip 1+ε_exp (1.0) for augmented samples and 1+ε_std for standard ones, plus a KL penalty; trained with EasyR1.

Navigation: build a 3D scene graph and occupancy map, expose Memory and Frontier image buffers, retrieve rules from D_exp, and let the VLM pick a frontier or memory node; a shortest-path follower (Habitat) or ROS nav stack executes it with max step 1.0 m.
Deployment: Qwen3-VL-2B/4B backbones, max 50 steps, real robot with client-server inference on an RTX 4090 (~2.7 s per step).

setting.backbone: Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct and Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct (fine-tuned with GRPO variant); Qwen3-VL-Plus used offline for data synthesis
setting.training_data: 14,526 synthesized sandbox trajectories with QA tasks and IF-THEN rules (7,988 HM3D from 698 scenes with benchmark-overlapping scenes removed, 6,538 InteriorGS); GOAT-Bench questions manually templated
setting.observation: panoramic RGB-D (120° HFOV multi-view captures) plus detected objects, 3D scene graph and occupancy map
setting.action_space: select a Frontier or Memory image node; a geometric planner executes it (max step 1.0 m)
setting.simulator: Habitat (HM3D scenes) plus InteriorGS Gaussian-splat sandbox; also a real robot
setting.privileged: none at test time (GT used only in sandbox training)

numbers_note: Real-world results are qualitative only, with no success-rate numbers. A-EQA is split-labelled 'val' since the paper uses a validation subset of OpenEQA A-EQA (not an official named split).
results: SAGE (Qwen3-VL-2B) reaches 53.2 SR† on A-EQA, above 3D-Mem with GPT-4o (52.6) and +8.9 over 3D-Mem with the same 2B backbone; the 4B model reaches 60.2 SR† / 47.2 SPL†. On GOAT-Bench, the 2B model reaches 56.7 SR (vs 46.4 for 3D-Mem 2B) and the 4B 64.8 SR, still below 3D-Mem GPT-4o (69.1).
limitations: Planner-assisted high-level method that depends on frontier generation, occupancy mapping and geometric execution rather than end-to-end control.
Limited to indoor quasi-static settings; VLM latency (~2.7 s per step) is a bottleneck, and the real-world evidence is small-scale and qualitative.
Experience rules are VLM-generated and noisy (10-18% incorrect in a manual audit), and main-text results use subsets of the benchmarks.
